races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Belicoso
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's hold-up juvenile holds the highest OR in the field at 81 and has placed once in three starts on good ground; at a mile this represents a step up in trip that could unlock more stamina, and a smooth passage from the rear will be essential given today's busy pace.|
runners_data.comment: Belicoso shaped with promise when third last time out and returns here fresh after a 35-day break, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour — the main question is whether he can finally convert, having been winless in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Margot Mae
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the ride on this Mrs Harrington-trained filly who has just one placing from three runs and only two similar-going efforts to draw on; she is a confirmed front-runner who will tangle with Seaxburh for the lead, and the question is whether she has the engine to sustain it over a mile.|
runners_data.comment: Margot Mae has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 92 — well clear of her official mark — suggests she is significantly better than her recent form implies, with a third two starts back keeping her honest; the risk is a trainer firing at just 3% over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Seaxburh
runners_data.note: O'Brien's other runner has placed three times from five starts, all on good ground, and her two recent second-placed efforts at seven furlongs and a mile give her arguably the most relevant form profile in the race; fitted with a hood in her last, she carries the most tactical experience of the front-runners and is the one most likely to convert pace into stamina.|
runners_data.comment: Seaxburh has been knocking on the door, finishing second twice and third last time out in her last three starts, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions to call upon. Winless in her last five, though her consistent placing makes her the one to beat off 135 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Razmataz
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's gelding has struggled to reach the frame in three starts and carries a fades-in-finish flag, making him a difficult proposition in a truly-run mile; his best chance is a slow pace that allows him to mask that weakness, which seems unlikely given the confirmed duelling front-runners.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Razmataz has experience of today's trip and conditions in his favour, yet his recent unplaced efforts are hard to ignore; the 128 lb burden from stall five adds a further test for a horse ranked sixth of eight.

runners_data.name: Maggie Walker
runners_data.note: David Marnane's filly is the only winner in the field, scoring on soft going over six furlongs at the Curragh, and her natural instinct is to race from behind — she has been mapped to midfield here because true hold-up room is scarce, which compresses her chance; if she can find a racing position closer than usual, her form profile makes her one to respect.|
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but beaten into sixth last time, and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Maggie Walker faces a stiff ask here; the 55-day absence adds to the query marks, though she does carry a manageable 127 lb from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Old Joanie
runners_data.note: James Barrett's filly carries an unknown style flag and has finished fifth, eighth and seventh from three starts at seven furlongs on good ground; her apprentice rider Rory Mulligan claims five pounds which is useful in a handicap, but the lack of a placing and a modest form string make her an outsider.|
runners_data.comment: Old Joanie has run over today's trip and going and arrives here 27 days on from her last start, with our rating of 74 suggesting she merits respect at this level from stall one carrying 127 lb; the concern is that she has been winless in her last three starts, with finishes of fifth, seventh and eighth to overcome.

runners_data.name: Elyatta
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's gelding has a fades-in-finish flag and has finished tenth, eighth and ninth in three runs on good ground, all at shorter distances — stepping to a mile with that profile gives little encouragement; he has been pushed into midfield on the map but his true inclination is to race from well off the pace, a role that looks harder to exploit here given the race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Elyatta has experience of today's trip and conditions to call upon, and 16 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; carrying 126 lb from stall four, he rates a mid-division prospect with more to find on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Fine Line
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's filly has never finished better than seventh across four starts, all on good ground, and carries both a fades-in-finish warning and a redistributed midfield position that masks her natural hold-up tendency; her OR of 63 is the lowest in the field, and without evidence of improvement it is hard to construct a scenario where the pace shape suits her.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a string of unplaced efforts making her hard to fancy from stall 2, Fine Line is ranked bottom of the field on our figures; experience over today's trip and going at least counts for something.

races.paceDynamic: Margot Mae and Seaxburh are the two confirmed front-runners in this eight-runner nursery, and with both likely to push for the lead from the gates, this mile will be run at an honest, pressured gallop rather than a dawdle. Seaxburh has placed three times at seven furlongs and a mile on good ground and will not easily surrender the rail, while Margot Mae's handler will want her prominent from the outset — the duel between them sets up a genuine test of stamina for two-year-olds at this trip. With the pace honest and sustained, the race shape broadly favours horses who can travel economically just off the speed and finish with a turn of foot, making a prominent-to-midfield profile the most advantaged. Maggie Walker, Elyatta, and Fine Line are genuine hold-up types who are mapped to midfield here because the rear of the field is already overcrowded; of the three, Maggie Walker — the only one with a winning form line and the most credible recent profile — is best placed to benefit if she can secure a better berth than her redistributed position suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Margot Mae and Seaxburh burn each other off up front, the race falls to a horse travelling just behind them who can pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Seaxburh's repeated placed efforts at this trip on good ground mark her as the most likely front-runner to sustain the effort, but a horse sitting a length or two behind the duel — such as Belicoso or Old Joanie — could time a run to perfection as the pace-setters tire inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters — most likely Seaxburh — seizes a clear early advantage and the other capitulates, allowing controlled fractions.
scenarios.body: Seaxburh has placed five times including twice at a mile on good ground and has the tactical experience to switch off once in front; if Margot Mae fades after the early duel, Seaxburh's stamina and placed consistency make her hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Type Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a horse from off the pace finds clear running in the straight.
scenarios.body: Maggie Walker is the only runner in the group with a win to her name and, though shuffled toward midfield by redistribution, her hold-up tendency suits a strongly-run mile if gaps appear; Belicoso's trainer record and OR of 81 gives him claims under this scenario too.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner commits fully and the early gallop is deceptively moderate, compressing the field into a bunched sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow-burning mile on good ground at Killarney can catch out inexperienced juveniles who misjudge the tempo; Old Joanie's unknown style element and Razmataz's inconsistency make them each capable of getting involved opportunistically in a compressed finish, though neither has the profile to inspire confidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Seaxburh or Margot Mae blinks first in the battle for the lead — if neither concedes inside the first two furlongs, the winner is almost certain to come from off the pace as both tire.

Maggie Walker's redistribution from hold-up to midfield is the key positional story to monitor at the start; if Luke McAteer can secure a better-than-mapped pitch, her winning form gives her a meaningful upgrade in chance.

Belicoso's Joseph O'Brien trainer strike rate of 7/57 over the last 14 days is strong for the yard, and a step up to a mile for a hold-up horse could be exactly the trip switch that unlocks him — watch how Dylan Browne McMonagle positions him on the turn.

Seaxburh runs in a hood again having worn headgear last time; watch whether it keeps her settled behind the early duel rather than fighting for the front, which would be the optimal execution of her placed form at this trip.

Razmataz and Fine Line both carry fades-in-finish flags and together represent dead weight at the rear — their presence means genuine hold-up runners like Maggie Walker may find the back of the field more congested than the map suggests.

races.name: CSG Rated Race

runners_data.name: Mayflower
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact course and distance on Good ground 23 days ago — that form is directly relevant, though the hold-up style means she is reliant on a strong enough gallop to reel in those ahead; Jack Kearney (3) riding, no wins or places on similar going in recent visits before that win.
runners_data.comment: Mayflower landed a win in her last five starts and has experience of today's trip and going, giving her a solid foundation here; a run of mid-field finishes since is the slight concern, though her rating of 95 marks her as the one to beat from stall four carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Do For Love
runners_data.note: 127 days off the track is a significant fitness query for Gary Carroll and K J Condon, who have sent him back in reasonable trim (tongue tie), but his one win on similar going came over this trip at Slane and he will look to press on from a prominent position early.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and open to improvement, Do For Love won three starts back and, returning from 127 days off carrying 139 lb from stall two, she remains a filly with untapped potential.

runners_data.name: Kirkland Sioux
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at this trip on Good ground in his last two starts make him the most in-form runner in the field; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for the powerful Joseph O'Brien yard (7 winners from 57 in 14 days) and he is proven to travel prominently and quicken — the profile fits this race shape very well.
runners_data.comment: Kirkland Sioux has won twice in her last six starts, including back-to-back victories two and three runs back, and has experience over today's trip and going, but she was unplaced last time out and her rating of 69 leaves her with plenty to find on these terms.

runners_data.name: Manton Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has finished second or third three times in six Good-ground starts, though yet to convert that consistency into a win on this surface; runs without headgear for the first time, and Luke McAteer will need to find a clear run from an unpredictable style rating given his uncertain mapping.
runners_data.comment: Manton Bay catches the eye with a second last time out and a winner five starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before — the main risk is carrying 139 lb from stall seven on a mark of 87.

runners_data.name: Oscar Nominee
runners_data.note: Lightly raced but two-from-two at ten furlongs on Standard ground — stepping back to a mile on Good is a noteworthy combination of unknown factors; Ben Coen takes the ride for J P Murtagh (2/28 in 14 days) and 165 days off track makes fitness hard to assess, though the form on debut win was strong.
runners_data.comment: Oscar Nominee showed fair recent form — a winner two starts back and runner-up last time — but 165 days off the track is a significant fitness concern, and our rating of 67 leaves her well below the top end of this field.

runners_data.name: Iamimmaculate
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners a horse who is a natural front-rank racer by inclination, though the crowded prominent group means he is unlikely to secure that position today — his recent Good-ground placed effort is the most applicable piece of form, but racing back from a compromised spot tempers the outlook.
runners_data.comment: Iamimmaculate has shown consistent form in recent starts, finishing second last time out and a winner four starts back, and he has experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 135 lb from stall three is the chief weight query for a gelding rated 83.

runners_data.name: Totally Puzzled
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, whose last win came over this exact trip on Good going 96 days ago for Henry De Bromhead; Ronan Whelan gets an uncontested lead and the key question is whether he can sustain his advantage when the field quickens in the final two furlongs after a comfortable gallop.
runners_data.comment: Totally Puzzled faces a stiff task on our figures, ranked seventh of eight in the field, though she does bring a win from her last three starts and has run over today's distance and going before; the 96-day absence is a further concern.

runners_data.name: Elmakaya
runners_data.note: D K Weld's charge has placed twice from four runs on Good ground at this trip and is naturally a forward-travelling horse, but the crowded prominent positions push him into a midfield slot he will find uncomfortable — his consistency on Good going is genuine, yet the positional squeeze is a real tactical obstacle today.
runners_data.comment: Elmakaya has been knocking on the door, finishing second and then third in her last two starts before a fourth last time out, and she has experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Totally Puzzled is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, is set to stride out from the front at a controlled, self-dictated tempo over this one-mile trip on Good ground at Killarney. Do For Love, Kirkland Sioux, and Oscar Nominee are the natural prominent types who will look to track closely behind, but the field contains more pace-hungry horses than positions available — Iamimmaculate and Elmakaya are genuine prominent racers who are unlikely to find their natural spot and have been mapped back into midfield as a consequence. The result is a race where Totally Puzzled controls the tempo without meaningful pressure, setting a sustainable gallop that will not burn off the closers too early but will suit those who can travel fluidly in the first two or three positions. This race shape squarely favours hold-up horses with a sharp late turn of foot and, critically, prominent racers quick enough to hold a front-rank berth, while Iamimmaculate and Elmakaya face the tactical disadvantage of being shuffled back from their preferred roles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Totally Puzzled Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Totally Puzzled is allowed to stride comfortably in front unchallenged and sets a fair but unhurried gallop that suits hold-up finishers.
scenarios.body: Totally Puzzled dictates every yard at a pace he chooses, giving the race a single-file, controlled shape that stretches in the final two furlongs; horses with a genuine turn of foot off a genuine pace — Kirkland Sioux and Manton Bay — are positioned to finish past a potentially flattened leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Hit Their Stride
scenarios.trigger: If Do For Love and Oscar Nominee push up aggressively early, forcing a stronger gallop and taking the race away from a lone front-runner.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected pace develops with several horses competing for the front rank, compressing the field and suiting those with tactical speed and stamina; Kirkland Sioux, with two recent wins at this trip on Good going, and Oscar Nominee both thrive in a strongly-run race off a prominent berth.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses suddenly in the final furlong and the field concertinas, leaving a gap for a horse coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Mayflower, who won last time at this course and distance on Good ground, gets a tow into the race and produces her run widest of all; the controlled tempo created by Totally Puzzled paradoxically plays into the hands of one genuine hold-up type who has been biding her time on the outer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Iamimmaculate or Elmakaya manage to force their way forward despite the congested early pace, creating a messy, pressured race.
scenarios.body: Should either horse succeed in overcoming their positional disadvantage and push forward past their mapped midfield slot, the resulting scrimmage unsettles the race shape and opens the door for a prominent racer already well-placed; Kirkland Sioux's consistent record on Good ground and with a strong jockey booking gives him the resilience to handle chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch Kirkland Sioux's early positioning — if Dylan Browne McMonagle slots him directly behind Totally Puzzled in second or third, he becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given his two-win Good-ground form at this trip.

Monitor Do For Love's fitness signals in the paddock and early going — 127 days off the track with Gary Carroll pushing forward from a prominent position could see him fail to sustain his effort, or alternatively be used aggressively and disrupt the pace shape.

Watch for Iamimmaculate and Elmakaya scrimmaging for position in the first two furlongs — if both attempt to force forward from their remapped midfield slots, the early stages could be surprisingly competitive and the tempo could spike earlier than Totally Puzzled's connections would want.

Oscar Nominee's stamina for one mile on Good ground is untested — all form is at ten furlongs on Standard, and Ben Coen may need to ride him conservatively to see the trip out, which could limit his ability to press from a prominent berth.

Mayflower's headgear (hood, previously worn) and young age as a three-year-old with Jack Kearney (3) aboard means early-race behaviour and the draw could dictate how easily she settles and gets the run she needs late.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Vincent O'Brien Ruby Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Cristal Clere
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old front-runner with solid recent form including a Hea win in spring, but stepping back to 1m and meeting Hardy Warrior head-on means her stamina edge is neutralised; 63 days off is not ideal and similar-going stats show no wins from four placed efforts.
runners_data.comment: Cristal Clere landed a winner three starts back but has since finished ninth and sixth, and 63 days off the track raises freshness questions; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 135 lb from stall nine is the challenge he faces returning to form.

runners_data.name: East Hampton
runners_data.note: David Marnane's 4-year-old drops from 7f sprint company and the hold-up style looks awkward in this race shape; 0 wins from 8 runs on Good going is a concern, though the step up to 1m is new and McAteer could find a position slightly closer than expected.
runners_data.comment: East Hampton shaped with promise when second three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going, combined with a rating of 114 that ranks him ahead of all rivals, makes him a leading danger; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from a pair of disappointing efforts.

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 8f on Good at Gowran in his last completed run, giving him a solid profile here; Stephen Thorne's 0/5 T14 stat is modest but 19 days fresh and a course-distance compatible profile make him an interesting runner in behind the pace.
runners_data.comment: Jagged Edge shaped with promise when third two starts back and landed a win four starts back, and at 135 lb from stall 2 he retains solid claims on today's distance and going — the risk is that two unplaced efforts since that victory leave his form looking patchy.

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Settled prominently and finished second over 8f on Good earlier this season, which is precisely the distance and going combination here; Robson De Aguiar's T14 of 2/14 shows some activity and Wayne Lordan is a strong booking, though a 55-day absence needs proving.
runners_data.comment: A second three starts back and a winner six starts back in recent form, Carolina Jetstream brings distance and going experience into this, and her official rating of 105 makes her a genuine threat from stall one carrying 130 lb; the concern is a 55-day absence and two modest efforts since that placed finish.

runners_data.name: Quebec
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's hold-up 4-year-old returns after 89 days off and has failed to win any of seven runs on Good ground; Declan McDonogh is a high-quality partner but the long absence, below-par similar-going record, and hold-up style in a pace-honest race combine to limit confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Quebec arrives 89 days since her last run and has shown little encouragement recently, with back-to-back eighths and an unplaced effort; a third four starts back is the sole bright spot, and distance and going experience offers limited consolation.

runners_data.name: Rion Rubette
runners_data.note: Has won twice at 7f on Good and Soft recently, showing sharp, shorter-distance form, but his natural hold-up style is squeezed out by the cluster of closers in this field — the redistribution to midfield is a genuine concern, and the step up to 1m is unproven territory for him.
runners_data.comment: Rion Rubette shaped well on her latest start with a second, but an unplaced effort two starts back and our figures ranking her tenth of eleven make her hard to fancy, though she does return fit on 14 days' rest and has experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Subsonic
runners_data.note: Murtagh's 4-year-old won over 10f on Soft and has all his best form over longer distances, making 1m a potential trip concern; the tp headgear is retained, but his true closer's instinct is compromised by the busy rear of this field, and a 9-day turnaround following a midfield run deserves respect as a fitness pointer.
runners_data.comment: Subsonic has experience over today's trip and conditions and showed she can win in recent starts, but four of her last five outings have yielded a fourth, seventh, eighth and third, suggesting consistency remains elusive; the 130 lb burden does her no favours either.

runners_data.name: Syzygy
runners_data.note: Daniel McLoughlin's 4-year-old has been consistently placed over 8-9f on Good, including a recent second at Cork, and the blinkers (b) suggest connections are trying to sharpen his response; a midfield position suits the shape if the pace genuinely burns and he's one of the more compelling off-the-pace profiles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Syzygy showed she can mix it when second two starts back, though a sixth three starts back tempers enthusiasm; she has run over today's distance and going, and 130 lb from stall four is the challenge to overcome.

runners_data.name: Hardy Warrior
runners_data.note: O'Brien's 3-year-old is the most compelling front-runner in the race — his Gowran 1m win on Soft backs up his form, McMonagle's aggressive front-running style in Listed company is a major asset, and the tp headgear confirms the yard is asking him to roll; 24 days since last run is straightforward.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Sun
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's lightly-raced 3-year-old, winner of her only 8f start on Good at Leopardstown, is the most unexposed runner here and Shane Foley retains the ride; she's a genuine hold-up performer and while the redistribution squeezes her natural position, her upside potential is higher than the odds might reflect if gaps appear.
runners_data.comment: Moonlit Sun won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing she can mix it at this level, and she has experience over today's trip and conditions; however, a stable operating at just 3% in the past fortnight is a significant concern, and her fourth last time out suggests she has questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Wearing Stars
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 3-year-old has an excellent record of placing over 7-8f on Good ground and the tongue-tie is retained; she's a prominent racer who finished second over 8f on Good last time, making her tactically well-placed in this shape, though the big drop in OR to 79 reflects she hasn't won.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Wearing Stars faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and draws stall three carrying 124 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Hardy Warrior and Cristal Clere are confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the off, ensuring this 1m Killarney contest is run at an honest, pressured gallop rather than the false crawl that can flatter hold-up types. Cristal Clere has age and form on her side but Hardy Warrior carries the more dangerous jockey in Dylan Browne McMonagle and is likely to assert supremacy in the battle for the rail, meaning neither will get a soft lead. Carolina Jetstream and Jagged Edge will press from prominent positions, adding further pressure through the middle of the race and ensuring the tempo does not drop, which compresses the advantage for pure closers. This race shape — contested pace, honest fractions on Good ground, prominent runners controlling the order — favours horses who can race in or just off the leading group and sustain their effort into the straight; true hold-up types face a genuine challenge because Rion Rubette, Subsonic, and Moonlit Sun are all redistributed from the rear — the field holds more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the back, and of those three, Rion Rubette and Moonlit Sun are best-placed to find any ground, but none are likely to get their natural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy Warrior and Cristal Clere cut each other's throats up front, allowing a prominent stalker to time a run from just off the pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other through honest fractions, softening both, while a horse racing third or fourth travelling smoothly pounces in the final furlong; Good ground at Killarney over 1m rewards sustained galloping ability over sprint acceleration.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy Warrior asserts dominance early, secures an uncontested lead, and dictates a controlled pace that allows him to quicken clear.
scenarios.body: McMonagle's positive ride gets Hardy Warrior to the front without burning too much petrol, and if Cristal Clere cannot live with the pace he sets, Hardy Warrior could ration his energy and deliver a strong finish; his recent Gowran 1m win on Soft gives him the form and fitness for this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a genuinely strong gallop that burns out prominent horses, creating a window for a midfield horse to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Syzygy or Quebec, having settled in midfield behind the scrimmage, could capitalise if the pace is hot enough to stop the prominent horses sustaining; Syzygy's consistent placed form at 8-9f on Good ground makes her the profile best suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle stages and a genuine late-run is rewarded, allowing redistributed hold-up horses to close from well off it.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Rion Rubette, Subsonic, and Moonlit Sun are all pushed out of their natural rear positions and unlikely to get far enough back to generate a telling finishing run; Moonlit Sun's unexposed profile is the only genuine upside case here.

watchPoints.text: Hardy Warrior and Cristal Clere — watch for an aggressive duel from the gates; if neither concedes the rail early, both could burn energy that benefits a stalker like Carolina Jetstream by the 2f pole.

Rion Rubette and Moonlit Sun — both are natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield positions; if Paddy Harnett or Shane Foley cannot find a clear run rounding the final bend, their finishing efforts will be blunted by horses ahead of them racing out of role.

Subsonic — the 9-day turnaround and drop from 10f to 1m invites questions about whether JP Murtagh's team are targeting a specific performance or simply taking a run; watch his pre-race market moves for clues.

Syzygy — blinkers applied and consistently placed at 8-9f on Good; if the front two burn each other up, watch whether Scott McCullagh tracks the pace from midfield and delivers a challenge wider around the field in the straight.

Carolina Jetstream — Wayne Lordan's ride from a prominent draw will dictate whether she gets the dream position just off the duelling leaders; if she travels smoothly through the first half mile, she becomes the most dangerous beneficiary of a contested pace scenario.

races.name: T1 Healthcare Handicap

runners_data.name: Golddream
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who won at Gowran on Good ground 23 days ago wearing a visor (hg:v); David Marnane's operation is 0/14 in the last fortnight, and Golddream needs a strong gallop to bring a late run to bear — the solo leader scenario makes that uncertain.|
runners_data.comment: Golddream showed his best when winning five starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going keeps him firmly in the mix off a mark of 75; the worry is his unplaced run last time out casts doubt on current form.

runners_data.name: Saga Lucia
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here, ridden by Jamie Powell for an in-form O'Callaghan yard (2/12 over 14 days); limited form in similar going (0W0P in three tries) but the tactical gift of a clear lead on Good ground is a meaningful advantage regardless.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Saga Lucia arrives 34 days on from a sixth-placed effort and has run over today's trip before, though a string of mid-to-rear finishes and a speed rating of 60 suggest she faces a stiff ask from stall four carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Casamorati
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien-trained hold-up type with a persistent tendency to fade in the finish; Good-ground figures are poor (0W0P in three runs) and the extra mile trip is untested in recent form — Dylan Browne McMonagle will need a strong pace to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Casamorati shaped with real promise when second last time out, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives fit on 21 days' rest with a case on our rating; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts and needs to find more consistency.

runners_data.name: Glitter And Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Shane Foley aboard and an excellent record in similar conditions (8 runs on Good, three places); Harrington's yard is lightly represented over the fortnight but Glitter And Glory's profile — tracking the leader and quickening — maps perfectly onto this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Glitter And Glory shaped well when third three starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, with a rating of 81 suggesting she merits respect at the weights; the concern is a trainer firing at just 3% in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has placed three times in six Good-ground starts; McDonogh takes the ride after 43 days off, and while the fitness query is modest the horse's reliance on a truly run race to deliver a late run is the key concern here.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and third again four starts back, Chapel Lane has shown he can compete at this level and arrives here with a fitness edge after 43 days off; winless in his last five, he will need to find more, but as the top-rated runner in the field he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Sweet Baby Zou
runners_data.note: O'Brien's 7lb claimer Julian Pietropaolo partners this horse, who won at 10f on Good and holds genuine hold-up tendencies; pushed into a midfield mapping by the crowded rear-group, its chance is tempered by racing in an unfamiliar position — the fade flag compounds that concern.|
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but has disappointed since, and while she has run over today's trip and going, the 135 lb burden is a notable ask; a return to form at 21 days fresh cannot be ruled out, though recent efforts give little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Only One Scobie
runners_data.note: Won at Navan on Heavy and has been out of the frame repeatedly on Good ground (1W in 11 runs on similar); a true deep closer who finds himself mapped to midfield, meaning he must either hunt a gap from an unnatural spot or accept a wide passage — neither is ideal at OR 68.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner four starts back give Only One Scobie some earlier promise to cling to, but back-to-back unplaced efforts since are a concern, and a trainer without a winner in 25 outings over the past fortnight is a significant negative against him.

runners_data.name: Chirac
runners_data.note: Apprentice Paddy Harnett (5lb) partners this prominent racer for John James Feane; the form string shows a win at 7f on Soft and two places on Good going, and at OR 64 he carries least weight among the tracking types — likely to be ridden positively from a prominent pitch.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Chirac is hard to fancy at these weights off a mark of 64, and his record in recent starts — a fourth last time out, with a sixth three starts back — offers little encouragement, though the second two starts back and experience over today's trip and going provide slim positives.

runners_data.name: Sancerre Rock
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this horse, who is 70 days between runs and wears both tongue-tie and pads (hg:tp); a natural hold-up racer whose true role cannot be expressed from a redistributed midfield position, and the complete absence of wins in four outings on Good leaves the form thin.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Sancerre Rock has at least run over today's distance and going before, but a 70-day absence, a trainer firing at just 5% recently, and a run of poor efforts make him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: John La Bear
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's gelding won at Naas on Yielding/Soft but faded on his latest Good-ground run and is tagged with a finish fade warning; Ben Coen takes the ride, and while the 21-day turnaround is fine, Good ground has produced four non-wins in nine tries — a natural closer in an overcrowded back half.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and officially rated 62, John La Bear arrives on the back of an unplaced effort and faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a win in his last five starts shows he can find the line.

races.paceDynamic: Saga Lucia is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no credible challenger likely to press her hard from the outset, she should be able to settle into a comfortable, controlled gallop around the Killarney mile on Good ground. Glitter And Glory and Chirac will track prominently just behind, meaning the pace is real but not frantic — a sustainable tempo that keeps the race honest without burning off those travelling in behind. The bulk of the remaining field are genuine hold-up types (Golddream, Casamorati, Chapel Lane, Sweet Baby Zou, Only One Scobie, Sancerre Rock, John La Bear), but the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear, and Sweet Baby Zou, Only One Scobie and Sancerre Rock are redistributed to midfield, meaning the late-running end of the field is genuinely congested. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader on a sustainable tempo — classically favours prominent racers who can track the pace, receive a soft lead, and quicken at the right moment; true deep closers face a tactical puzzle if the gallop never truly tests the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saga Lucia Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Saga Lucia dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the race is run to suit prominent raiders.
scenarios.body: Saga Lucia sets fractions that are fair but never punishing, and Glitter And Glory or Chirac, sitting in her slipstream throughout, are perfectly positioned to pounce once the turn is negotiated; prominent types get first run and enough time to quicken on Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to stretch the field and a prominent racer delivers a powerful mid-race move.
scenarios.body: Glitter And Glory — with strong Good-ground form and Shane Foley's positional judgement — or Chirac attacks before the hold-up horses can organise their challenge; the winner is already two lengths clear before the closers find daylight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the leader and open a clear late-running lane.
scenarios.body: Golddream or Chapel Lane, the truest hold-up types in the field, are produced with a late run if the tempo quickens mid-race; they need the leaders to have done real work, which a single front-runner on a comfortable gallop may not guarantee.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Profit
scenarios.trigger: If congestion behind the leader creates scrimmaging and one of the out-of-role midfielders benefits from a gap.
scenarios.body: Sweet Baby Zou, Only One Scobie or Sancerre Rock would need to find a clear run from an unnatural position and hope the pace collapses; their STYLE_FIT penalties and form make this the least likely shape to deliver.

watchPoints.text: Glitter And Glory is ideally positioned to exploit the uncontested lead — watch whether Shane Foley slots in second or third immediately, because any race where she travels smoothly on the heels of Saga Lucia becomes very difficult for closers to peg back.|

Saga Lucia's ability to control the fractions is critical: if Jamie Powell is forced to quicken too early by pressure from Glitter And Glory or Chirac, the pace could spike mid-race and open the door for Golddream or Chapel Lane from behind.|

With Sweet Baby Zou, Only One Scobie, Sancerre Rock and John La Bear all compressed into a midfield cluster, the stretch turn at Killarney is likely to be congested — watch for traffic issues that could eliminate the genuine late runners before they get a clear run.|

Chirac at OR 64 with a 5lb claimer is the lightweights' representative among the prominent types; if Harnett positions boldly early and gets cover from Saga Lucia, the low weight could prove a bigger factor than the rating suggests in a race where the leader controls the tempo.|

races.name: Kellihers Toyota Kingdom Gold Cup Handicap

runners_data.name: Taipan
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner given a solo lead here; OR 96 is the joint highest and Shane Foley rides, but last-five form shows predominantly mid-to-rear finishes at longer trips on softer ground, and a style-fit flag suggests this front-running role is out of character — treat the lead as tactical rather than a genuine strength.
runners_data.comment: Taipan arrives here as the top-rated runner in the field and bounced back to second last time out after a rough patch, showing he retains ability at this trip and going; the main concern is a trainer operating at just 3% over the last fortnight, while he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Eagle Fang
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with an excellent good-ground profile (9/15 sim-going) and three wins from six placings in similar conditions; Chris Hayes takes the mount and the horse's recent third at 17f and second at 14f on good show he stays and handles this trip well — a prime tracker candidate.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and placed three starts back, Eagle Fang arrives in good nick after 25 days off, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; he carries 136 lb but the overall profile makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Granite Bay
runners_data.note: Jack Cleary (5) claims here for Fahey who has no runners in the 14-day window; the horse has placed at 16f on good before and his form figures of 42-437 show consistency without a win breaking through — capable of making the frame if the pace is honest.
runners_data.comment: Granite Bay shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back and second four starts back, and he returns after 25 days in good order with experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and dropped to seventh most recently.

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey Andrew Slattery combination is rare and noteworthy; a genuine hold-up type whose two recent seconds at 13f and 16f on good ground show he stays and finishes strongly, though a worrying 15th last time out at 16f on good tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: A second two starts back hints at residual ability, and she has experience over today's trip and going, but a sixth last time out and a trainer strike rate of just five per cent in the past fortnight are significant drags on confidence at 134 lb.

runners_data.name: The Real Screamer
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this five-year-old who has won twice at shorter trips and steps back out to 16f where a recent fourth came; the prominent style suits a tracking role just off Taipan, and good-ground form (1/12f/GOO, 1/10f/GOO) is encouraging even if the trip is a slight query.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures and representing a trainer without a winner in 25 attempts over the past fortnight, The Real Screamer is hard to fancy despite back-to-back wins three and four starts back; unplaced last time out, only the going experience and 21-day gap offer any encouragement.

runners_data.name: Factual Fact
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's record of 4/38 in 14 days is context; this horse is a natural front-runner — he won at 17f on good and placed at 14f in similar conditions — but the crowded prominent group means he is mapped to midfield, a position that blunts his natural advantage and warrants a discounted assessment.
runners_data.comment: Factual Fact arrives with strong claims, having won three starts back and finishing second on three other occasions in recent starts, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the main risk is a return from 54 days off.

runners_data.name: Light Up The Dark
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's yard sends Dylan Browne McMonagle, one of Ireland's most in-form riders; his one win came at 14f on soft and prominent style suits tracking, but his most recent run was a disappointing ninth at 17f on good, making the form slightly unreliable at this distance.
runners_data.comment: Landed a winner three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, but that ninth last time out is a concern; she carries 133 lb here, and with a rating of 95 she sits mid-division of thirteen in what looks a competitive contest.

runners_data.name: War Rooms
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan partnership for Gerard Keane; a hold-up type who won last time out over 13f on good, but his form at 16f is poor (13th, 20th) suggesting the extra yardage on a flat track may stretch his stamina — the pace profile in a Taipan-led race may not suit him.
runners_data.comment: War Rooms won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but four of his last five outings have been unimpressive, and 133 lb is a stiff ask for a gelding rated 89 officially.

runners_data.name: Immutable
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer by nature, placed twice on soft at 12f, but this field's depth at the head of affairs forces him into an unnatural midfield role; Gary Carroll rides for a trainer without a recent winner (0/3, T14) and the horse's one good-ground sim run produced no placing — conditions and position both work against him here.
runners_data.comment: Consistent but winless, Immutable has finished second in each of his last two starts and brings solid recent form into this, though he is yet to score in his last five and faces a stiff ask from 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Gaoth Chuil
runners_data.note: The 7lb claim from Reese Holohan helps offset the OR 77, and this eight-year-old has won twice recently (1/17f/GOO and 1/15f/GOO) — the best recent winning form in the field over similar trips on the same going; a true hold-up type who could be the most dangerous late finisher if the pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Gaoth Chuil won two of her last five starts but comes here on the back of an unplaced effort 23 days ago, and a mark of 77 leaves her with something to find on our rating; she has run over today's trip and going, at least bringing relevant experience to the table.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's yard has been in productive form (7/20, T14) and Luker's Tipple has won three of his last five starts including at 16f and 18f on good — a highly relevant profile; naturally wants to be prominent but the congested early order means he is likely held up against his wishes, diluting what is otherwise a strong claims profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Luker's Tipple faces a stiff ask here, with a seventh last time out and an unplaced run two starts back doing little to inspire confidence; going experience and a trainer firing at 35% in the past fortnight are the few crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Sir Jeremy
runners_data.note: Youngest runner in the field at four; Noel Meade's hold-up type who won last time at 12f on good but has no form beyond that trip in recent runs — a significant step up to 1m6½f for a horse whose flat speed over shorter may not translate here.
runners_data.comment: Sir Jeremy won last time out and is back quickly enough on going he has encountered before, but ranked last of the 13 runners on our figures, he looks up against it here despite that recent victory.

runners_data.name: Chutzpal
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's second runner; a natural front-runner with four wins from seven good-ground starts (14/15 sim-going) and proven form at 14-18f — the most prolific good-ground course-type in the field, yet the redistribution into midfield strips away his natural weapon, and a 7lb claimer (Conor Cusack) adds risk despite the headgear flag.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last three starts and ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Chutzpal is hard to fancy at present, though he has run over today's trip and going before and does carry a manageable 119 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Taipan is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should stride into an uncontested, controlled gallop from the outset over this 1m6½f trip on good ground at Killarney. The pace will be honest but measured — Taipan's connections can dictate fractions without being pressured, making this a classic sit-and-sprint test for those tracking in behind. Factual Fact, Immutable, Luker's Tipple, and Chutzpal are all natural prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred position in a field this crowded at the head of affairs, meaning several will be shuffled back into an unfamiliar midfield role against their nature. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently just off the leader or who possess a genuine sustained staying kick from mid-division — a clean, uncontested lead at a good-ground pace almost always sets the race up for a quality closer or a handy tracker to pounce in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Taipan Controls, Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Taipan bowls along uncontested and the pace is genuine but not suicidal, setting up a fair test.
scenarios.body: Taipan's controlled solo lead draws the field along at an even clip, leaving enough energy for the race to be decided by class and position in the home straight; horses tracking prominently in the first two or three will have first run on the closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Finishers Surge Home
scenarios.trigger: If Taipan's gallop is just fast enough to drain the leaders and the hold-up horses get a smooth passage through.
scenarios.body: A true pace develops and genuine hold-up types, finding clear daylight in the straight, produce the best late work; the extra 1m6½f on good ground amplifies stamina, rewarding horses who have been conserving energy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field allows Taipan to set an uncharacteristically slow tempo and no one applies pressure until too late.
scenarios.body: With no rivals willing or able to challenge for the lead, Taipan is gifted a sprint finish against tired rivals who have burned energy racing through the field; the horse with the softest lead in the race dominates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramblers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution resolves itself chaotically early and several natural prominent types race wide and keen, inflating the tempo.
scenarios.body: A messy early order forces horses like Factual Fact and Luker's Tipple to race harder than ideal, compressing the field and turning this into a test of raw class over staying power; a high-OR horse who lands a handy pitch in the chaos benefits.

watchPoints.text: Gaoth Chuil — won his last two races at 17f and 15f on good ground specifically, making him the most in-form stayer under these exact conditions; if the pace is genuine from Taipan, watch for Reese Holohan (7) to angle him widest late and produce the best sectionals in the field.

Luker's Tipple — three wins from five in similar distance/going combinations is exceptional form, but Robert Whearty must decide early whether to push for position or settle; if trapped in traffic against his natural style, his chance evaporates despite the strongest raw profile.

Eagle Fang — if Chris Hayes can slot in second or third on the rail behind Taipan, this horse's six-placing record on good ground makes him extremely dangerous in the straight; watch whether he gets that berth or is squeezed by the crowded prominent group.

Factual Fact and Immutable — both are natural front-runners mapped to midfield; if either attempts to push forward aggressively in the first half-mile to reclaim their preferred position, it will inflate the tempo and fundamentally reshape the race, turning a tactical test into a stamina grind.

Taipan's fractions in the opening half-mile will define this race — if Shane Foley dictates a slow tempo, hold-up horses like Gaoth Chuil and Royal Hollow will be left with no meaningful pace to aim at and must produce their own finish from further back than ideal.

races.name: Killarney Towers Hotel & Leisure Centre Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Lady Plimsoll
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly who has placed at 16f on Standard and 12f on Good, she shaped well enough in her last two runs for O'Callaghan to suggest she handles this trip; returning just three days after her last run is worth noting, though her sim-going record of one win and three places at Killarney-equivalent conditions gives confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and well-treated on her last five starts, Lady Plimsoll has run over today's trip and going and arrives just three days after finishing second, suggesting she is in good heart; winless in recent starts, she must convert her placings, but on a rating of 77 she tops these ratings.

runners_data.name: Trubshaw
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, she won at 14f on Good and rates as the single pace-setter in this field; her STYLE_FIT flag at 0.94 is irrelevant here — she is not racing out of role, she is the natural leader, and that uncontested position gives her a tangible tactical edge.|
runners_data.comment: Trubshaw's win came five starts back and he carries 136 lb into this, but he has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 70 puts him as a genuine threat here; the risk is that his recent form has been well below that level.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: This genuine hold-up performer has solid form at 14-16f on Good, including wins and places; though the map shows him in midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, his natural instinct is to come from deep, and his STYLE_FIT tag reflects the constraint of a compressed field rather than any doubt about his ability.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten into eighth last time out and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Jurality is hard to fancy against this field despite the experience over today's trip and going, and a win in his last six starts; a trainer without a winner in 25 attempts over the past fortnight compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Numidia
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with two recent wins at 13f and 14f on Good, she has the proven stamina for this trip and the visor (headgear) suggests connections want her sharp; her hold-up style suits a well-strung-out race and her sim-going record in similar conditions is solid.|
runners_data.comment: Numidia won two of his last six starts and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going before, but that eighth last time out is a concern, and 132 lb is no easy burden for a horse rated 62 officially.

runners_data.name: Charlie Brow'n
runners_data.note: His best form came at 14f on Soft and he is yet to show his true hold-up style can be expressed in a field this top-heavy with similar types; his STYLE_FIT flag at 0.91 and the redistribution to midfield underscore that he is unlikely to get the deep position he needs.|
runners_data.comment: Charlie Brow'n won three starts back and returns in good order on 16 days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour; the risk is that he has to prove his two subsequent outings were just blips.

runners_data.name: Chicago Moon
runners_data.note: A three-year-old making his handicap debut over an extended trip having won at 12f on Good, his prominent style makes him one of the few runners genuinely suited to sitting just behind Trubshaw; De Bromhead's strong 14-day form strike (4/38) is an encouraging angle.|
runners_data.comment: Chicago Moon won last time out and has going experience to call on, but her three starts before that return just one third from four, and 39 days off the track leaves a fitness question to weigh against her recent peak.

runners_data.name: Espritroyale
runners_data.note: Consistent placer whose recent seconds at 10f and 14f on Soft suggest he stays well and handles varying ground; his Cromwell training yard is in excellent 14-day form (7/20) and a move up markedly in trip to 1m6½f looks the key test.|
runners_data.comment: Espritroyale has finished second in each of her last two starts and arrives here 21 days fresh, with experience of today's trip and going in her favour; a trainer firing at 35% over the past fortnight is a serious booster, though she remains yet to win and that final step up may again prove the stumbling block.

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran with modest recent form — finishing 20th and 4th in similar conditions — whose true hold-up style is further squeezed by redistribution; his OR of 55 is the joint-lowest in the field and his form string does not suggest he can compete at the business end.|
runners_data.comment: Desert Friend showed up with a win five starts back but has finished fourth twice and unplaced in between, making his recent form inconsistent; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 125 lb, and returns after 25 days off.

runners_data.name: Celestially
runners_data.note: A three-year-old with a second and a third at 14f on Good at Killarney proper, this O'Brien filly clearly stays the trip and handles the track; her hold-up style is a natural one and, though mapped to midfield by necessity, she is one of the likelier redistributed types to get a meaningful position if the field doesn't compress too hard.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Celestially is hard to fancy despite being placed two of her last three outings; she has run over today's trip and going before, and her 37-day absence suggests she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Astolat
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 14f on Good and handles the trip, but her OR of 56 is the lowest in the field and her redistribution to midfield reflects the overcrowding of hold-up types; Hogan's yard is active (2/22 in 14 days) but her profile suggests a minor role at best.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Queen Of Astolat faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 16-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Trubshaw is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to pressure her, she is highly likely to bowl along at a comfortable, controlled tempo over this 1m6½f trip on Good ground at Killarney. That sustainable gallop will almost certainly play to the benefit of closers and hold-up horses who can track a measured pace and finish powerfully into a race that never truly hotted up early. The field is overloaded with natural hold-up types — Lady Plimsoll, Jurality, Charlie Brow'n, Celestially, Desert Friend, and Queen Of Astolat are all genuine hold-up performers, meaning several will be forced to race closer than ideal simply by the compression of the field, and it is Jurality and Celestially who hold the strongest credentials to actually secure a forward-tracking position if they choose to. The tactical verdict is clear: a single uncontested front-runner setting a fair but undemanding pace strongly favours horses capable of tracking in the slipstream and producing a sustained late run, with genuine hold-up types best served if the pace is honest enough to string the field out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trubshaw Controls, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw leads unchallenged at a fair tempo and the race develops into a one-paced staying grind that rewards those tracking her.
scenarios.body: Trubshaw dictates a comfortable rhythm, the field settles in a compact group behind, and the final furlongs become a test of stamina where those closest to her have the advantage; Chicago Moon and Lady Plimsoll, both capable of racing prominently and finishing strongly over this sort of distance, are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw's pace is slow enough to bring the whole field into it and a sprint-style finish develops in the straight.
scenarios.body: A crawl early compresses the field and turns the race into a dash from two furlongs out, benefiting horses with a sharp turn of foot; Celestially's recent second at 14f on Good at Killarney and Espritroyale's consistent placed form give them the profile to finish over the top.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Trubshaw Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Trubshaw is allowed to stride out entirely unchallenged and builds such a commanding lead that hold-up types cannot bridge the gap.
scenarios.body: With no pressing rival, De Bromhead's mare converts front-running dominance into a wire-to-wire success, the field failing to organise an effective challenge from off the pace; this scenario depends on the tempo being truly dawdling so that the weight of numbers behind never gels into a coherent pursuit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Numidia Lands Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field, Numidia produces a big-field hold-up run similar to her recent wins at 13f and 14f on Good.
scenarios.body: Numidia has won twice in recent form and handles Good ground well over staying distances; the veteran mare gets a clean run through the field in the straight and swoops late in the manner of her best performances.

watchPoints.text: Watch Trubshaw's early gallop — if she hacks along unchallenged at a genuinely leisurely pace, the entire hold-up battalion will arrive in a wall and the result will be chaotic; the first two furlongs will dictate the shape entirely.
Chicago Moon is a three-year-old stepping sharply up in trip to 1m6½f for the first time; if he doesn't stay the extra distance, he could drop out tamely after briefly tracking the leader.

Numidia is wearing a visor for the first time (hg:v) — if the headgear produces an overexcited early display rather than the hold-up finish she needs, her chance evaporates in a race where the pace is already slow.

At least five runners — Jurality, Charlie Brow'n, Desert Friend, Celestially, and Queen Of Astolat — are redistributed hold-up types forced closer than ideal; watch for crowding and checking in the straight if the field compresses behind a slow-going Trubshaw.

Espritroyale's trainer Gavin Cromwell is in strong current form (7/20 in 14 days) and the step up to 1m6½f looks the right call given his two recent seconds over shorter; monitor market moves late on.

races.name: HR Buddy (Q.R.) Race

runners_data.name: Murat
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner, Peter Lawlor-trained, 43 days fresh — his two wins have both come on Good ground and his record of 4W4P at similar going makes him the natural race-shaper; the absence of any pace rival means he should get a perfect uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but that victory came 43 days ago and the layoff is a question mark, while our rating of 78 trails his official mark; he has going experience to call on, though the weight of 165 lb is no help to his claims.

runners_data.name: Ragmans Corner
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane's gelding ran creditably to finish 1st and 2nd in his two best recent efforts, but he is a true hold-up horse by style and finds himself pushed closer to the action than he would prefer because the rear positions are heavily congested; his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 is a material discount.
runners_data.comment: Ragmans Corner has shown admirable consistency, finishing third in three of his last five starts, and he has run over today's trip and going, while 22 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; the risk is that his two most recent efforts have been below that standard.

runners_data.name: Samui
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner returning after 405 days off — the long absence is the dominant concern here, but he has strong prominent-race form with five placings from 15 similar-going runs and the tongue-tie may help him travel; Hannah Smullen's 7lb claim helps offset the layoff penalty slightly.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, with three finishes of second, second and third in his last four, and experience over today's trip and conditions, Samui is a clear threat at a rating of 104 — though 405 days off the track is the significant unknown for a gelding yet to win in recent form.

runners_data.name: Can Happen
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR 120, with a course win on Good ground and a tongue tie fitted; Peter John Flood's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to collapse — Miss Georgie Benson takes 7lbs off and the trip looks fine, but his 9th last time suggests inconsistency.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and rated just 76 — sixth of eight on our figures — Can Happen faces a stiff ask under 158 lb, though he has run over today's going before and shaped with some promise when second last time out.

runners_data.name: Glowing Account
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' nine-year-old is a prominent-style runner with a win and place from only four Good-ground starts, and his last run (0) is worrying context; if he is right he is the obvious horse to track Murat and challenge two out, and Miss Townend's booking maintains yard confidence.
runners_data.comment: Glowing Account ran unplaced last time but returns after 23 days with his trainer firing at 38% over the past fortnight, and he has run over today's trip before; a rating of 108 makes him the one to beat, though he is yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Silas Marner
runners_data.note: Sabrina Harty's veteran has a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 — a natural hold-up horse racing out of role in this pace shape — and his recent form figures of 0, 18, 16 on similar going offer little encouragement; the 8-day turnaround is notably quick and the combination of misplacement and poor recent form makes him hard to support.
runners_data.comment: Silas Marner has run over today's trip and going, and at 79 on our rating he ranks as a genuine danger in this field, returning on a sharp eight-day turnaround; the concern is he is winless in his last four starts, with a ninth last time out among those struggles.

runners_data.name: Simpletwistoffaith
runners_data.note: John F O'Neill's nine-year-old returns from 294 days off with modest Good-ground form (0W1P from 15 runs) and a form string of 8, 6, 11, 8, 13 suggesting he is well below winning fitness; a hold-up style in a race where the rear is overcrowded adds further tactical difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to score in his last three starts, Simpletwistoffaith returns from a lengthy 294-day absence carrying 158 lb, but with so few runs on the board he remains open to significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Supreme Law
runners_data.note: Harty's second runner carries the lowest OR in the field at 40 and is tagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a triple handicap on his chances given he is also a redistributed hold-up horse with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 and no wins or places on similar going from seven attempts; the 15-day turnaround does little to change the picture.
runners_data.comment: Supreme Law has been winless in his last four starts, finishing ninth most recently, and with an official rating of 40 he faces a stiff ask against this field; experience on today's going offers faint encouragement, but the weight of 158 lb does him no favours.

races.paceDynamic: Murat is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest his lead, he should stride into an uncontested position from the outset over this 2m1f trip at Killarney on Good ground. He has won over similar distances on Good going before and the lack of pace pressure means he can dictate a controlled, measured gallop that maximises his stamina and gives him every chance to steal a decisive margin turning for home. Glowing Account and Samui are the most plausible chasers from a prominent pitch, tracking Murat through the early and middle sections, while Can Han, Simpletwistoffaith, Ragmans Corner, Silas Marner and Supreme Law — three of whom are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield because the rear is overcrowded — will be deployed further back than ideal. This race shape heavily favours the front-runner and those who can sit close without burning fuel: a lone leader on a sound surface sets a true but comfortable gallop, and the profile most likely to prevail is the pressing prominent type who sits second or third and can strike when Murat comes back to the field, or Murat himself if allowed to control the tempo throughout. Note that Ragmans Corner, Silas Marner and Supreme Law are genuine hold-up horses compressed into the midfield picture because there is simply no room at the true rear, which compromises their chance in this pace shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Murat Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Murat dictates an uncontested, relaxed gallop and is never seriously pressured into the home straight.
scenarios.body: Murat sets his own fractions from the front, conserves energy through the middle portion of the race, and simply has too much in reserve when kicked for home at the top of the straight; his two Good-ground wins at similar trips underline this profile exactly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Murat's lead is modest enough that a tracking prominent runner gets a tow into contention and outstays him on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Glowing Account or Samui, sitting a length or two off Murat through the final circuit, gets the ideal lead to aim at and produces a stronger finish than the front-runner; Good ground and a sound gallop suits a horse who travels prominently and has a clean jumping record.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Murat goes too fast early and the pace collapses in the straight, opening the door for a late runner from the rear.
scenarios.body: Can Happen, the highest-rated hold-up type with a course win on Good ground, would be the most likely beneficiary if the front-runners come back to the field in the final two fences; however, Ragmans Corner, Silas Marner and Supreme Law are true closers forced into midfield and racing out of role, which undermines this scenario's probability materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Murat is headed or checked early by a rival racing outside their comfort zone, creating a fractured, uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: An unsettled pace over 2m1f with several misplaced hold-up horses in midfield creates a bunched, scrappy finish where any runner can land a blow; Simpletwistoffaith or Supreme Law, gifted a much closer position than normal, could flatter but neither has the form to be a credible winner at their current ratings.

watchPoints.text: Murat's early sectionals are critical — if Mr H C Swan settles him on a genuinely relaxed tempo through the first mile, he becomes very hard to beat given the total absence of pace pressure from any rival.

Glowing Account's last run was a 15th-place finish and Willie Mullins runners returning from a poor effort can bounce back sharply or regress further — watch his travelling in the early stages as a leading indicator of whether he fires today.

Can Happen showed a 10th and a 9th in his two most recent runs despite an OR of 120; if he fails to travel smoothly from his deep hold-up position, Miss Benson may find herself with nowhere to go in a compressed midfield.

Three redistributed hold-up horses — Ragmans Corner, Silas Marner and Supreme Law — will be racing closer than their natural style demands, creating a risk of interference or traffic problems in the middle pack on the final circuit; runners passing them from behind should be tracked carefully.
The going is confirmed Good throughout the card at Killarney with no deterioration reported across seven races — conditions are consistent and no runner faces a late going surprise.
